_purpose: The "More info" words of the settings (framework SETTING-INFO-1), read by engine\pro-settings\Build-SISettingsCatalog.ps1 together with settings.descriptions.locked.json and composed into each catalog entry as `info` (engine\pro-settings\SI-SettingInfo.ps1): what it does, what happens ON / OFF (or when changed), risk and reversibility, what it requires, the default, the recommendation, the page on invardia.com, and -- for a destructive or security-reducing setting -- the value that needs a confirmation (confirmWhen: on | off | lower) and the words shown in it. Most of a setting's info comes from its help words; this file adds only what they do not say. "groupRisk": the risk sentence of a setting of that group that has no risk of its own. "settings": per setting any of risk, requires, recommended, whenOn, whenOff, whenChanged, confirmWhen, confirm. Every safety check (SI_Guard_*_Enabled / _Mail, SI_Guards_Enabled, SI_GuardMail_Enabled) gets its risk and 'confirm when off' by rule. Written from the code that reads each setting, 2026-10-09.

groupRisk.Mail & notifications: A wrong value can mean that alerts and reports go to the wrong people or to nobody, or that mail stops; no collected data is changed. Reversible at once: change it back.
groupRisk.Guards (safety checks): A safety check protects your data from a broken run; changing it changes when a step is held or stopped. Reversible at once.
groupRisk.Schedules & what runs: Changes when or whether jobs run: a job that does not run leaves its data older until it runs again. Reversible at once; nothing already collected is changed.
groupRisk.Collection scope & limits: Changes what is collected from the next run: narrowing it means some assets or data are not collected, so they look absent in profiles, CIs and reports (absence is never read as fixed). Reversible: change it back; the next run collects again.
groupRisk.Risk Analysis reports: Changes what the Risk Analysis reports show, how findings are filtered or scored, or where reports go, from the next run; earlier reports are unchanged. Hiding findings can make real exposure invisible to readers. Reversible: change it back.
groupRisk.Risk Analysis -- mails and executive vie: Changes how the headline figures are presented in the mails and the executive view; the findings themselves are unchanged. Reversible at once.
groupRisk.AI: Affects whether and how AI is used: when AI is used, asset data is sent to YOUR Azure OpenAI deployment, and it costs per call. Reversible at once; results already produced stay.
groupRisk.Sign-in & Azure resources: Affects how the jobs sign in or which Azure resources they use. A wrong value stops the affected jobs at their next run (nothing is changed or deleted); a broader identity or right gives the jobs more access than they need. Reversible: correct it and run again.
groupRisk.Advanced / diagnostics: A tuning or diagnostic setting: it mostly changes run time, cost or log detail. Leave it at the default unless support asks. Reversible at once.
groupRisk.Data & retention: Changes how long data is kept or how quickly assets are treated as gone. Shortening a retention DELETES older data at the next clean-up and that cannot be undone; shortening a grace period retires assets (and closes their findings) sooner. Lengthening is safe but uses more storage.
groupRisk.Connectors & CMDB: Affects what SecurityInsight writes to your CMDB or ticketing systems. Reversible for future runs, but changes already written there stay; the connector's own guards hold large or unsafe changes.

SI_Pro_DataQuality_Mail_Enabled.risk: Off: nobody is mailed when a key number of a run is far off its usual range; the warnings are still on the Data quality panel and in Run health. Nothing is ever held or stopped by them. Reversible at once.

SI_Pro_DataQuality_Mail_To.risk: A wrong address means the daily data-quality mail reaches the wrong people or nobody; nothing is held or stopped. Reversible at once.

SI_Pro_DataQuality_AssetDropPercent.risk: Only changes when a data-quality WARNING is shown and mailed; nothing is ever held or stopped by it. Reversible at once.

SI_DataHealth_Enabled.risk: Off: SecurityInsight no longer checks its own data, and nothing is held when the data goes wrong -- a short or wrong collection can reach tickets, the CMDB and the connectors. Reversible at once; it applies from the next daily check.

SI_DataHealth_Margin_EntraUsers.risk: Higher: more missing or different users are tolerated before data-out is held. Lower: data-out is held sooner. Reversible at once; it applies from the next daily check.

SI_DataHealth_Margin_EntraApps.risk: Higher: more missing or different apps are tolerated before data-out is held. Lower: data-out is held sooner. Reversible at once; it applies from the next daily check.

SI_DataHealth_Margin_Devices.risk: Higher: more missing or different devices are tolerated before data-out is held. Lower: data-out is held sooner. Reversible at once; it applies from the next daily check.

SI_DataHealth_Margin_Azure.risk: Higher: more missing or different Azure resources are tolerated before data-out is held. Lower: data-out is held sooner. Reversible at once; it applies from the next daily check.

SI_DataHealth_Margin_DefenderForCloud.risk: Higher: more differences in Defender for Cloud recommendations are tolerated before data-out is held. Lower: data-out is held sooner. Reversible at once; it applies from the next daily check.

SI_DataHealth_Margin_Vulnerabilities.risk: Higher: more vulnerabilities missing from the findings are tolerated before data-out is held. Lower: data-out is held sooner. Reversible at once; it applies from the next daily check.

SI_DataHealth_Margin_RiskAnalysis.risk: Higher: more differences between a report and Defender are tolerated before data-out is held. Lower: data-out is held sooner. Reversible at once; it applies from the next daily check.

SI_DataHealth_MarginMinimum.risk: Higher: small sources tolerate more differences before data-out is held. Lower: small sources are stricter. Reversible at once; it applies from the next daily check.

SI_Telemetry_SendHealth.risk: On: the daily data health counts go to Invardia (no names or ids); an Unhealthy install then holds the update ring from moving on. Off: Invardia does not know the data health of this install. Reversible at once.

SI_Pro_SourceDropout_HoldDeliveryDays.risk: Higher, or 0: mails and ticket updates keep going out although one source's data is that many days old. Lower: delivery waits sooner when a source stays down. The calculation is never held by it, and nothing is closed or retired by it. Reversible at once.

SI_Pro_Pipeline_GoOnAfterFailedStep.risk: Off: after one failed step the web app gets nothing from that run -- a new install stays empty until its first run completes. On: the web app shows what the completed collections brought, marked as not complete. Either way nothing is closed, no ticket is changed and no mail is sent from a run that is not complete. Reversible at once; it applies from the next run.

SI_Pro_PublishPartialRun.risk: On: a run in which a report fell back to its last complete result is shown, marked -- a page can then show a part from an earlier run. Off (the default): the pages keep the last complete run until a run completes in full, so a newer result can wait a day. Nothing is closed or sent by it. Reversible at once; it applies from the next run.

SI_Pro_Pipeline_FirstRunRestarts.risk: 0: a step that fails on a new install's first collection is not started again, so the first data arrives a run later. Higher: a step that cannot succeed is tried that many times more before the warning. Nothing is written to a CMDB, to ServiceNow or to a ticket by a restart, and nothing is closed. Reversible at once; it applies from the next run and only until the first complete collection.

SI_Pro_LifecycleStaleOpenRepair.risk: count changes nothing. apply changes finding records once: an empty CI id is cleared, and a finding still open under an old asset key that is open under its CI is closed as rekeyed -- its CI's own record stays open, so no finding disappears from the open list; it only stops being counted twice. Not reversible by the setting (turning it off later does not reopen them); nothing is deleted.
SI_Pro_LifecycleStaleOpenRepair.recommended: off; count first when support asks, then apply.

SI_Pro_SourceDropout_AssetDropAction.risk: Accept: a source that answered only in part is taken as the truth at once -- the assets it no longer lists are marked not seen, and their CIs retire after the usual days. Confirm (the default) costs one run when a clean-up is real. Reversible at once; it applies from the next collection.

SI_Pro_DataQuality_ReportDropPercent.risk: Only changes when a data-quality WARNING is shown and mailed; nothing is ever held or stopped by it. Reversible at once.

SI_Pro_DataQuality_FillDropPoints.risk: Only changes when a data-quality WARNING is shown and mailed; nothing is ever held or stopped by it. Reversible at once.

SI_Pro_DataQuality_TierShiftPercent.risk: Only changes when a data-quality WARNING is shown and mailed; nothing is ever held or stopped by it. Reversible at once.

SI_DataOut_Outputs.risk: Changes which workbooks and ServiceNow hand-offs are written from the next data sync; an output switched off stops being refreshed, what it wrote before stays where it is. Reversible: switch it on again.
SI_DataOut_Outputs.recommended: Leave it empty for the default outputs; name the outputs you need.

SI_DataOut_ServiceNowCiTable.risk: Rows go to the named ServiceNow Import Set table; a wrong table name means the rows land where no transform map reads them. Reversible at once.
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowCiTable.requires: The servicenow-ci output switched on (SI_DataOut_Outputs) and the ServiceNow connection.

SI_DataOut_ServiceNowRequest.risk: A resync sends every record in scope again in one batch; a test batch sends at most 5 rows per output that the importer never imports. Carried out once per token; nothing is deleted.
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowRequest.requires: A ServiceNow output switched on and the ServiceNow data-out connector.

SI_DataOut_ServiceNowStagingStatusTable.risk: Set to a table that does not exist on the instance, nothing is sent to ServiceNow until it is there (the ServiceNow check says why). Empty, your importer cannot tell a finished push from one that stopped halfway. Reversible at once.
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowStagingStatusTable.requires: A ServiceNow output switched on (SI_DataOut_Outputs), the ServiceNow data-out connector and the table created in ServiceNow.

SI_DataOut_ServiceNowVulnTable.risk: Rows go to the named ServiceNow Import Set table; a wrong table name means the rows land where no transform map reads them. Reversible at once.
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowVulnTable.requires: The servicenow-vulnerable-item output switched on (SI_DataOut_Outputs) and the ServiceNow connection.

SI_Cmdb_Run.risk: apply writes to your ServiceNow CMDB on every run; plan writes nothing. Reversible for future runs; what was written stays in ServiceNow.
SI_Cmdb_Run.recommended: plan until the match report shows what you expect.

SI_RA_Findings.confirm: Every Risk Analysis Detailed run will also copy its findings per CI to Log Analytics (SI_Finding_CL). On a large estate the copy takes hours and the run ends only when it has ended; it adds ingestion cost.
SI_RA_Findings.risk: Longer Risk Analysis Detailed runs and Log Analytics ingestion cost for every finding, every run. SecurityInsight itself does not need the copy. Reversible: turn it off and the next run copies nothing.
SI_RA_Findings.recommended: Off, unless your own workbooks, Sentinel rules or KQL read SI_Finding_CL.

SI_Cmdb_AllowCreate.confirm: SecurityInsight will create CIs in your ServiceNow CMDB for assets it could not match.
SI_Cmdb_AllowCreate.risk: New CIs are created in ServiceNow (with apply and the create-if-unmatched mode); created CIs stay when it is turned off again.

SI_VulnSync_Run.risk: plan stops every vulnerability connector from writing or closing anything until it is cleared; nothing is lost, the next run catches up. Reversible at once.

SI_Telemetry_SetupControls.risk: Changes only what Invardia sees about this install's setup; nothing in your tenant changes. When Invardia does not take the full list ('all'), the report goes again once with the minimum list; the daily status report and the run reports are not affected. 'off' means Invardia cannot see a missing setting and offer help.

SI_Telemetry_SendEndpoints.risk: Changes only what Invardia sees: the web app's and the MCP server's addresses; nothing in your tenant changes. Reversible at once.

SI_AssetTagging_Enabled.risk: The tagging rules you have switched on take devices out of every report (a tag ending in --Excluded--SI). A wrong rule hides many devices at once. Reversible: turn it off and the next CI build puts them back.
SI_AssetTagging_Enabled.recommended: Off until you have decided which automatic exclusions you want; then on, and check the Excluded assets report.

SI_AssetTagging_Apply.risk: Writes to your tenant: every run changes Defender machine tags, Azure resource tags and Entra custom security attributes. A wrong rule tags or untags many objects at once. Reversible only by changing the rules and running again (or by hand); the audit trail records every change.
SI_AssetTagging_Apply.recommended: Off until the report-only output has been reviewed; then on.

SI_Pro_AssetTagging_Apply.risk: Writes to your tenant: the job changes Defender machine tags, Azure resource tags and Entra custom security attributes. A wrong rule tags or untags many objects at once. Reversible only by changing the rules and running again (or by hand); every change is on the audit trail.
SI_Pro_AssetTagging_Apply.requires: The asset tagging identity's write rights (granted by setup only when asked).
SI_Pro_AssetTagging_Apply.recommended: Off until the report-only plan has been reviewed on the Asset tagging page; then on.

SI_Bootstrap_GrantTaggingRoles.risk: Gives the asset tagging identity WRITE rights in your tenant (Defender machine tags, Azure tags, Entra security attributes). Reversible: remove the role assignments; turning the setting off does not remove rights already granted.
SI_Bootstrap_GrantTaggingRoles.recommended: Off unless asset tagging should write; then on for one setup run.

SI_CVE_RequireExploit.risk: Hides every vulnerability without a known exploit from the reports: real, patchable exposure becomes invisible to readers. Reversible at once (the next report shows them again).

SI_DumpAIPayload.risk: Writes the prompts and the asset data sent to AI to files on disk, where they stay until removed. Reversible: turn it off and delete the files.
SI_DumpAIPayload.recommended: Off; on only briefly when support asks.

SI_LoadPendingRules.risk: Unreviewed, AI-drafted rules change tiers and findings: wrong tiers or noisy findings can follow. Reversible: turn it off; the next run uses reviewed rules only.
SI_LoadPendingRules.recommended: Off; review pending rules and approve the good ones instead.

Mail_SendAnonymous.risk: Mail is sent without signing in to the mail server: only safe through an internal relay that accepts mail from this host alone. With an open relay, report mails can be spoofed or intercepted. Reversible at once.
Mail_SendAnonymous.recommended: Off (sign in to the mail server, or use the shared mailbox).

AutomationFramework.risk: On a normal install this breaks sign-in: every engine takes its identity from an internal platform that is not there, and runs fail. Reversible at once.

SI_DisableEndpointAzureCorrelation.risk: Azure VMs and Arc machines lose the link to their endpoint record, so one machine can show two different tiers. Reversible at once (the next run links them again).

SI_Bootstrap_UseClientSecret.risk: Every job carries the client secret: a secret to store, rotate and protect, and queue scaling is not available. A supported choice, but weaker than a managed identity. Reversible: run setup with the managed identity.

SI_RebuildAuthBlock.risk: The next setup run REPLACES the sign-in block in your configuration file with fresh values from Key Vault. Wrong Key Vault values stop every run until corrected. Reversible from a configuration backup.
SI_RebuildAuthBlock.recommended: Off; on once after rotating a secret.

SI_DisableTranscript.risk: No run log is kept: a failed run cannot be investigated afterwards and support has nothing to read. Reversible at once (from the next run).

SI_RequireMdeActive_Endpoint.risk: Drops every device known only to Exposure Management or Entra (some Azure VMs, personal and IoT devices): those devices disappear from profiles and reports, and their exposure with them. Reversible: the next run includes them again.

SI_RequireRecentSignIn_Identity.risk: Drops every identity without a recent or available sign-in, including privileged accounts that are rarely used: they disappear from profiles and reports. Reversible: the next run includes them again.

SI_Pro_DataSync_DryRun.risk: No run data reaches the Pro database: the web app's pages stop getting new data while it is on. Reversible: turn it off; the next sync catches up within its look-back.
SI_Pro_DataSync_DryRun.recommended: Off; on only to check a new setup safely.

SI_Pro_CmdbSql_DryRun.risk: The CMDB table is not updated while it is on: consumers of the CMDB hand-off keep the last state. Reversible: turn it off.
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_DryRun.recommended: Off; on only to check a change safely.

SI_Trend_DryRun.risk: No trend rows are written while it is on: the trend line and weekly history get a gap for every such day, which cannot be filled later. Reversible from the next day.

SI_EnableAI.risk: Asset data (names, properties) of assets the rules cannot place is sent to YOUR Azure OpenAI deployment, and each call costs. Reversible at once; tiers already set by AI stay until the next full run.
SI_EnableAI.recommended: Off unless rules leave many assets untiered.

SI_EnableAI_azure.risk: Resource data of untiered Azure resources is sent to YOUR Azure OpenAI deployment, and each call costs. Reversible at once.
SI_EnableAI_azure.recommended: Leave it off and use AI integration (on = on for all engines); this only turns the Azure engine on alone.

SI_EnableAI_endpoint.risk: Device data of untiered devices is sent to YOUR Azure OpenAI deployment, and each call costs. Reversible at once.
SI_EnableAI_endpoint.recommended: Leave it off and use AI integration (on = on for all engines); this only turns the endpoint engine on alone.

SI_PrivilegeTierClassifier_RunAI.risk: With the Azure OpenAI settings set, new role and permission names are sent to YOUR Azure OpenAI deployment, and each call costs; off leaves new ones untiered for manual review. Reversible at once.
SI_PrivilegeTierClassifier_RunAI.recommended: Keep the default; turn it off only to keep AI out of this engine.

SI_DisabledAssets_Collect.risk: Disabled accounts and devices disappear from profiles, CIs, reports and connectors from the next run; their open findings and tickets are kept (never closed). Reversible: the next run collects them again.

SI_DisabledAssets_Correlate.risk: Disabled assets are not built into CIs from the next run; findings of existing CIs are kept (never closed). Reversible: the next run correlates them again.

SI_DisabledAssets_RiskAnalysis.risk: On adds findings for disabled accounts and devices to the reports: more rows to read. Off is the default; the two reports where the disabled state is the finding always include them. Reversible at once.
SI_DisabledAssets_RiskAnalysis.recommended: Off, unless you are cleaning up disabled accounts and devices.

SI_DisabledAssets_StateActions.risk: On lets the lifecycle resolve and close findings and tickets of disabled assets like any other, and a finding that is missing for a disabled asset can then be closed. Reversible for future runs; what was closed stays closed.

SI_DisabledAssets_Connectors.risk: On sends disabled accounts and devices to your CMDB, ticketing systems and exports. Reversible for future runs; records already written there stay.

SI_CiBuild_FullReconcileDays.risk: None to the data: a change to what the CIs are built from always rebuilds every CI on the next run; the setting only decides how often an unchanged estate is rebuilt in full. Reversible at once.

SI_CiRulesBudgetSeconds.risk: None to the data either way: an asset that is not fully evaluated keeps its last complete result, and no tier or finding is based on part of the rules. A very high value, or 0, lets one asset hold the build and with it the steps after it. Reversible at once.

SI_PrivilegeTierClassifier_RefreshDays.risk: None to the data: a changed role or permission always rebuilds the catalog on the next run; the setting only decides how long an unchanged catalog is kept. Reversible at once.

BuildSummaryByAI.risk: Report content is sent to YOUR Azure OpenAI deployment for a summary, and each run costs. Reversible at once.
BuildSummaryByAI.recommended: As your organisation prefers; on gives readers a written summary.

SI_RiskAnalysis_BuildSummaryByAI.risk: Report content is sent to YOUR Azure OpenAI deployment for a summary, and each run costs; a run stops if Azure OpenAI is not configured. Reversible at once.

SI_InvardiaUpdate_Enabled.risk: No updates are applied any more -- including security fixes -- until it is turned on again. Reversible at once.

SI_Update_RenameDisplayNames.risk: SecurityInsight's applications and the SQL admin group keep their earlier names, unlike a new installation. Nothing else changes. Reversible at once.

SI_LicenseRequest_Auto.risk: The licence is not renewed automatically: when it expires, Pro features stop until a licence is installed by hand. Reversible at once.

SI_Mail_SmtpKept.risk: Low: only the advice to move to a shared mailbox is hidden; how mail is sent does not change, and a failed test mail still shows in red. Reversible at once (Undo on Settings > E-mail).
SI_Mail_SmtpKept.recommended: Off, unless you keep your own SMTP relay on purpose.

SMTP_UseSSL.risk: Report mails (with asset and finding details) travel unencrypted to the mail server: only acceptable on an internal relay. Reversible at once.

SI_CollectDefenderRecommendations.risk: Defender for Cloud recommendations are no longer collected: those findings disappear from the reports (they are not fixed). Reversible: the next Azure run collects them again.

SI_EnableSignInEnrich.risk: Sign-in counts, apps and locations stay empty: findings that depend on sign-in activity lose that context. Reversible: the next run collects it again.

SI_IncludeFirstPartySpns.risk: Microsoft-published service principals are left out -- including privileged ones, whose exposure then disappears from the reports. Reversible: the next run includes them again.

SendToLogAnalytics.confirm: Every Risk Analysis run will also copy its report rows to Log Analytics (SI_RiskAnalysis_Detailed_CL; SI_RiskAnalysis_Summary_CL for the Summary report; the trend row in SI_Trend_CL). On a large estate the copy takes close to an hour after each run; it adds ingestion cost.
SendToLogAnalytics.risk: Log Analytics ingestion cost for every report row, every run, and a longer run on a large estate. SecurityInsight itself does not need the copy: its pages, the data sync, the vulnerability connectors and the trends read the database. Reversible: turn it off and the next run copies nothing.
SendToLogAnalytics.recommended: Off, unless your own workbooks, Sentinel rules or KQL read the report rows in Log Analytics.

SI_RiskAnalysis_SendToLogAnalytics.confirm: The Risk Analysis jobs made at setup will copy their report rows to Log Analytics after every run; it adds ingestion cost.
SI_RiskAnalysis_SendToLogAnalytics.risk: Log Analytics ingestion cost for every report row, every run. SecurityInsight itself does not need the copy. Reversible: Copy Risk Analysis report rows to Log Analytics turns it off again.

AutoBucketCount.risk: Large queries run at a fixed split and can exceed Defender's row limit: reports on big estates can be incomplete or fail. Reversible at once.

SI_RA_PartsInParallel_Max.risk: Only changes how many parts of a report are asked from Defender at a time, so how long Risk Analysis takes: 1 makes a large report take much longer; a higher number can make Defender ask SecurityInsight to slow down more often (it then does). The findings are the same either way. Reversible at once.

SI_SqlPacing_Enabled.risk: Off: on a busy database the large writers keep it at its limit for as long as the daily run writes, and the web app is slow meanwhile. No data is changed either way. Reversible at once.

SI_SqlPacing_HighPercent.risk: Only changes how soon the large writers slow down: a lower value gives the web app more room and makes a full run take longer on a busy database. No data is changed. Reversible at once.

SI_SqlPacing_LowPercent.risk: Only changes when the large writers go back to full pace. No data is changed. Reversible at once.

SI_Pro_DataRetentionDays.risk: A shorter value PERMANENTLY deletes older history (trends, past collections) at the next sync; current state is kept. Cannot be undone. Longer grows the database and its cost.
SI_Pro_DataRetentionDays.recommended: Keep 90 days or longer for trends across quarters.

SI_Pro_AuditRetentionMonths.risk: Setting it, or lowering it, PERMANENTLY deletes audit rows older than this at the next sync (at least 13 months is enforced). Cannot be undone; check your audit obligations first.
SI_Pro_AuditRetentionMonths.recommended: Not set (keep the audit trail), or your audit policy's period.

SI_Pro_ConfigBackupRetentionDays.risk: A shorter value deletes older configuration backups at the next backup run (pinned ones are kept). Cannot be undone.

SI_Pro_ConfigJournalRetentionDays.risk: Setting it, or lowering it, deletes older change-journal rows at the next backup run. Cannot be undone.

SI_LogRetentionDays.risk: A shorter value deletes older run logs: past runs can no longer be investigated. Cannot be undone.

SI_Cmdb_RetireAfterDays.risk: A lower value lets a CI retire sooner after its asset was last seen -- a device that is only offline for a few days can lose its CI (in the CI table and in ServiceNow). A CI retired by mistake does not heal by itself until the asset is seen again. Reversible for the future.
SI_Cmdb_RetireAfterDays.recommended: 7 days (the brake against CIs retired by mistake).

SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays.risk: A shorter grace period retires unseen assets sooner -- and closes their open vulnerabilities as retired. A device that is only offline for a while can be retired by mistake. Reversible for the future; closed findings reopen only when the asset is seen again.
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays.recommended: 30 days (devices can be offline for weeks).

SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_AzureResour.risk: A shorter grace period retires unseen Azure resources sooner and closes their open vulnerabilities as retired. Reversible for the future.

SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_AzureVm.risk: A shorter grace period retires unseen Azure VMs sooner (a stopped VM can be retired by mistake) and closes their open vulnerabilities as retired. Reversible for the future.

SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_ClientPc.risk: A shorter grace period retires unseen client PCs sooner (laptops are often offline for weeks) and closes their open vulnerabilities as retired. Reversible for the future.
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_ClientPc.recommended: The general value (30 days) or longer.

SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_Server.risk: A shorter grace period retires unseen servers sooner and closes their open vulnerabilities as retired. Reversible for the future.

SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_ServicePrin.risk: A shorter grace period retires unseen service principals sooner and closes their open findings as retired. Reversible for the future.

SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_User.risk: A shorter grace period retires unseen users sooner and closes their open findings as retired. Reversible for the future.

SI_ActiveStaleDays.risk: A shorter value marks more assets inactive: devices not seen within it leave the profiles and reports (a device offline for a week or two can drop out). Reversible: the next run includes them again.

SI_CVE_MaxPublishedAgeDays.risk: Any value above 0 hides older CVEs from the reports: old unpatched vulnerabilities -- often the most exploited -- become invisible to readers. Reversible at once.
